subject: Flowdown coordination: MSA redlines, subprocessor attestation & DPA annex
messages:
From: Samantha Reyes <samantha@cloudplus.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Flowdown and DPA for Redwood MSA / order form

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Before legal signs the order form we need a quick alignment on two items that are blocking procurement: a) subprocessor flowdown obligations for any downstream vendors that handle CloudPlus customer data, and b) an updated DPA annex that maps to our standard audit/retention requirements.

I attached our standard security questionnaire and a sample clause we typically ask for. Can your team confirm whether Redwood can: 1) provide an up-to-date subprocessor list with attestation, 2) accept a DPA annex (we prefer an annex that sits alongside the MSA), and 3) include a limited carve-out process for logging/analytics vendors where full flowdown would be operationally infeasible?

Timeline: procurement needs a path to signature by next Friday (7/16). If helpful, we can set a short legal-to-legal call.

Attachments: CloudPlus_Security_Questionnaire.pdf

Best,
Samantha Reyes
Head of Procurement | CloudPlus Inc
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Reyes <samantha@cloudplus.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Flowdown and DPA for Redwood MSA / order form

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear summary and the questionnaire. Looping in our legal lead (Lauren) to drive the redline review.

High-level from sales: we can provide a subprocessor list and an attestation form; we typically implement a DPA annex that tracks the MSA but need to confirm a few specifics around the carve-outs you mentioned for logging/analytics. To keep this moving, I am attaching the current MSA redline we've been using for similar customers and a draft subprocessor annex that legal can refine. Can Lauren propose concrete edits and a short mutual action plan (MAP) so we can align timelines?

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_proposed_redline_v2.pdf; Subproc_Annex_Draft.docx

I'll also open a HubSpot deal note for the procurement deadline.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Reyes <samantha@cloudplus.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Flowdown and DPA for Redwood MSA / order form

Hi Samantha — thanks, and nice to meet you (virtually). I've reviewed the questionnaire and Sean's redline. Summary of our ask and proposed path: 

1) Subprocessor list and attestation: we can provide a current list and a signed attestation confirming we require subprocessors to implement comparable controls. We will not publish live credentials but can provide vendor name, type, location, and SOC/ISO evidence where available. We attach our standard attestation template — please confirm that format works.

2) DPA annex: we accept an annex modelled as an appendix to the MSA. Our standard language covers retention, encryption (at-rest/in-transit), data locality, and breach notification timelines. A few CloudPlus items to confirm: a) audit rights (we can provide SOC reports and a compliance pack; on-site audits are limited), b) KMS ownership (we support customer-managed keys on private deployments; for hosted, we use Redwood KMS but can provide key separation options for enterprise plans), and c) subprocessors performing logging: we generally flow down obligations but can apply a tailored control set for telemetry vendors that process only anonymized logs.

3) Carve-out process: rather than a blanket carve-out, we propose a formal exception process: vendor-level risk assessment + documented compensating controls + procurement sign-off. This keeps legal comfortable while giving CloudPlus operational flexibility.

Next steps we propose: legal-to-legal call (30 min) tomorrow or Friday to go through redlines and produce a signed MAP with milestones (attestation, final redline, DocuSign). I've attached a redlines summary with line-number references and our attestation form.

Attachments: Redlines_Summary.txt; Subproc_Attestation_Form.xlsx

If the carve-out process looks acceptable, we can aim for signature within your timeline; otherwise list the specific logging vendors you anticipate and we can triage exceptions quickly.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
From: Diego Torres <legal@cloudplus.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Reyes <samantha@cloudplus.com>, procurement@cloudplus.com
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2027 07:11:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Flowdown and DPA for Redwood MSA / order form

Thanks Lauren — helpful summary. A few reply points from CloudPlus legal: 

• Subprocessor evidence: SOC reports are fine; where SOC is unavailable we ask for a signed tech attestation and at least one supporting control artifact.

• Audit rights: on-site vendor audits are rare for us; we are comfortable with SOC2 + access to compliance artifacts.

• Logging/analytics carve-out: we appreciate the exception process. For speed, can Redwood accept a narrow enumerated exception for specific logging vendors (we will share names) while we gather attestation materials? Our procurement team will not sign without that narrow exception captured in the order form.

Attached are our markups to the proposed flowdown language. We can discuss on a call, but alternatively we can proceed with DocuSign if we reach quick alignment. DocuSign routing link: https://docusign.com/DocuSign/ID=ABC123

Attachments: CloudPlus_proposed_flowdown_markups.pdf

Regards,
Diego Torres
Senior Counsel | CloudPlus Inc
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Diego Torres <legal@cloudplus.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Samantha Reyes <samantha@cloudplus.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Flowdown and DPA for Redwood MSA / order form

Diego / team — thanks for the markups. From Redwood legal's perspective we are comfortable proceeding provided the following are satisfied before signature: 

1) CloudPlus provides the list of specific logging/analytics vendors to be carved out (we will evaluate each; expect at least a 3-business-day triage).
2) CloudPlus accepts our attestation format for any vendor without SOC evidence; evidence must be submitted within 10 business days post-signature.

If those two items are acceptable, we will instruct sales to proceed with DocuSign after legal clears the final pass. Monica — can you confirm operationally that we can collect attestation artifacts post-signature and escalate any gaps to Risk?

If yes, Sean please proceed to route the DocuSign link to procurement and update HubSpot.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Lead Contracts Counsel | Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Reyes <samantha@cloudplus.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Diego Torres <legal@cloudplus.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Flowdown and DPA for Redwood MSA / order form

Thanks Kimberly — that process works for us. We'll send the list of logging vendors by EOD (expect 2 names) and accept the attestation workflow. We will route the DocuSign envelope once we receive the final redline. One question: can you confirm whether the attestation can include KMS key ownership options (we may want customer-managed keys depending on the deployment)?

I'll aim to have the vendor list and procurement routing confirmed today so we can hit the signature target.

Best,
Samantha Reyes
Head of Procurement | CloudPlus Inc
